 It feels like 'open season' for Man Utd published at 22:33 BST 22:33 BST 
 FT: Como 4-1 Manchester United 
 Matt Upson 
Former Arsenal defender on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 What teams aren't in better shape and form than Manchester United? Manchester United for me get results because they spent a lot of money and they do have players that can do things, and they will win some football matches, but at the moment it's just open season it feels at the club.
 That's a very difficult thing to deal with, can you be successful on the pitch when that's going on? Probably not, I don't think that's possible. I wasn't surprised to see that they really struggled against a team that's on the complete opposite side of where they are. 
 [Como are] together, fresh, new, have something to prove and grabbing their opportunity as a group. 
 There is something definitely wrong, and to criticise not the manager directly, but the tactics, which land at his feet is so damaging.
 17 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'A fascinating game' published at 22:31 BST 22:31 BST 
 FT: Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal 
 Arsenal 
 Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta, speaking to TNT Sports: "That is one of the highest levels we played. Two teams who wanted to press each other and wanted to attack and wanted to play. It was a fascinating game. 
 "We started the game incredibly well, we were so dominant. Then we had to adapt without Saka. In the second half the game was a bit even and they scored the goals and we had to react, which we did. We scored and we had the chance to win it too. That is the level."
 On Saka's injury: "They are a bit concerned. A player who has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see."

Former Chelsea and England midfielder on TNT Sports 
 Bruno Fernandes is absolutely questioning the tactics. 
 I've played for managers where I don't agree with the tactics that they do but you might say that to your mate or to your wife... you don't come out as captain of the club and question the manager. 
 He doesn't even do it properly. If you're going to come out [and say that] be bold and say it with your chest. 
 He sort of says 'it could have been this but then it's up to the manager to decide'.

 Kasper Schmeichel 
Former Celtic goalkeeper on 5 Live 
 With experience you learn that you need to keep these things in-house. It's a problem, with everything that happened during the week.
 Michael Carrick didn't need this, the club didn't need this, and what it is, is that it's exposing all of the issues that are at Manchester United. 
 It's very plain to see that there are loads of issues but you need to be fixing them, you need to be having meetings within the club, which I'm sure that they are, but it's obviously not resolved because there are some frustrations there which haven't been resolved. 
 It's just translating on to the pitch.

 'Kane is the clear winner of Ballon d'or' published at 22:20 BST 22:20 BST 
 FT: Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal 
 Arsenal 
 Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice, speaking to TNT Sports about Harry Kane for Ballon d'Or: "He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves, the year he has had has been remarkable. When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.
 "He is ridiculous, such a good player and I am lucky I can play with him, not so lucky I have to play against him."
 On his goal: "When you play against teams who are man to man all over the pitch you have to apply certain principles. They follow you all over the pitch but I lost my man and I just kept running and lot my runner and then I was in on the goal. So happy. Gyokeres has been making such a good impact coming off the bench. He made some great runs tonight and set me up for the goal.
 "It is what the manager has drilled into us. We aren't just going to come here and sit. At home they are probably one of the best teams in Europe so to come here tonight and give that account of ourselves was really good. We have to keep going."

Former Celtic goalkeeper on 5 Live 
 I have been in situations myself where you feel as a player the management or the club isn't aligned from top to bottom. 
 You kind of feel lonely out there and I think that's what Bruno Fernandes is doing, he's reacting to maybe feeling alone out there. I watched him in the game, he's trying to press, he turns around and there wasn't anybody following him up. His reaction, his body language wasn't great when those situations occurred. That's frustration. 
 But, I also do think that given this last week and what's happened, he probably should not be saying these things because it's only going to add to the problems.

 By Alex Howell Football reporter at the Allianz Arena Declan Rice scored a late equaliser as Arsenal and Bayern Munich played out an entertaining draw in the league phase of the Champions League in a game where Bukayo Saka limped off with injury. 
 Saka went down after just 10 minutes with a suspected thigh problem, after he attempted to play a pass without anyone around him.
 Eberechi Eze replaced Saka and scored the opening goal of the game in the 35th minute, after he latched on to an excellent pass by Martin Odegaard, with the video assistant referee needing to intervene after the England international was initially flagged offside.
 But Bayern Munich were behind for just 10 minutes, with Harry Kane picking the ball up in midfield and splitting the Arsenal backline with a pinpoint pass for Alphonso Davies to finish.
 Kane, who had produced a number of eye-catching passes during the match, then put Bayern in front from the penalty spot.
 The England captain's shot struck Jurrien Timber's hand inside the area and Kane sent David Raya the wrong way from 12 yards as he looked to have completed the turnaround. 
 Bayern piled the pressure on to Arsenal as they looked for a third goal but the Gunners held firm before Rice exchanged passes with substitute Viktor Gyokeres and drilled a low shot into the bottom corner to level the game. 
 The Gunners pushed for a winner and Jurrien Timber forced Manuel Neuer into an acrobatic stop before full-time. 
 Figure caption, 'This could be a real problem for Arsenal tonight and going forward'
 Another all-action performance from Rice - Arsenal player ratings 
 Figure caption, Eze puts Arsenal ahead after perfect pass from Odegaard
 Starting XI 
 David Raya: A very good save down low from a Serge Gnabry shot in the first half and an even better one from Dayot Upamecano in the second. His long-range passing was a big weapon for Arsenal in this match. 7 
 Jurrien Timber: Looked like he had regained some of his old sharpness. Some good moments going forward but got caught for one of the Bayern goals. 6 
 Ezri Konsa: The centre-back was given the tough task of sticking close to Harry Kane and had to follow the striker all over the pitch. A decent performance but also booked for a late tackle. 7 
 Gabriel Magalhaes: A solid game from Gabriel but part of a backline that conceded twice. 6 
 Riccardo Calafiori: The left-back is usually known for his attacking ability but he put in a good defensive display even though Arsenal conceded twice. 7 
 Declan Rice: The usual all-action display from Rice and he capped the performance with an excellent equaliser. 8 
 Bruno Guimaraes: The midfielder still looks like he is getting up to speed after joining the club. Some nice moments on the ball and almost scored with a header. 6 
 Martin Odegaard: An excellent pass for the opening goal and looked bright all evening. 7 
 Bukayo Saka: Started brightly but had to be withdrawn after just 10 minutes as he picked up what looked like a thigh injury, going down when nobody was near him as he attempted a pass. 5 
 Noni Madueke: Started on the left but switched to the right and was direct all night. Lots of effort and bright moments but nothing to show for it. 6 
 Kai Havertz: Some nice moments of link play but not enough of an attacking threat. 6 
 Subs: 
 Eberechi Eze (on 10, Saka): Scored the opening goal with a great finish low into the corner. A much-needed goal. 8 
 Viktor Gyokeres (on 68, Havertz): Came on and exchanged passes with Rice for the equaliser. 7 
 Myles Lewis-Skelly (on 69, Guimaraes): A big game to come on in from the bench and did well. 6 
 Mikel Merino (on 85, Odegaard): Introduced as Arsenal looked for a winner. 6 
 Subs not used: Meslier, Arrizabalaga, White, Mosquera, Zubimendi, Dowman.
